objective: Test whether autocorrelation-robust trend uncertainty can withhold false drift decisions while retaining useful decisions.

protocol.base: SG041 frozen predecision gate, correlation-matched spectral-null decision and stopping times unchanged.
protocol.estimate: From only samples observed at the decision's stopping time, split into consecutive non-overlapping groups of 10, compute median per group, fit centered ordinary-least-squares trend, divide slope by 10 for per-observation units.
protocol.uncertainty: Newey-West HAC covariance on OLS score x*residual, Bartlett weights at lags 1,2,3; standard error of slope divided by 10; interval slope ±1.645*SE (nominal 90%, not guaranteed in short time series).
protocol.decision: If SG041 confirms drift, retain only when HAC interval excludes zero. If SG041 rejects drift, retain only when entire HAC interval lies inside [-0.0032,+0.0032]. Otherwise abstain. Never turn an unresolved SG041 result into a positive or negative claim.
protocol.cost: same SG041: 0.06 per observation, 150 false-confirmation, 90 false-rejection, 18 abstention.
protocol.scope: Retrospective at current stopping time only; no extra observations requested, and original SG041 label preserved separately.

pilot.disclosure: Inspected before freezing; SG042 withheld one false rejection and four correct labels in this pilot; no claim of improved loss.

limitations: HAC short-sample normal intervals are not guaranteed to have nominal coverage under high persistence or nonstationary correlation.
Estimator based on same observations and binning as original trend; no source independence.
One chosen z and lag after pilot, no out-of-distribution guarantee.
Unresolved classifications represent withheld decisions, not correct predictions.
